<reason>Side B (PRO) built the stronger path to victory by framing the motion as prioritization rather than replacement, establishing that "encounter is a precondition for education," and effectively countering Side A's budget and editorial independence attacks. B's demographic argument about securing future relevance and the clarification that youth are saturated with commercial content rather than public service directly addressed the proposition's "remain relevant" clause. While Side A made strong points about universal service for the digitally excluded and the depth requirements of public broadcasting, B neutralized these by noting existing channels already serve those groups and that short-form can extend existing investigations at low marginal cost. Side B's execution cost from the clipped Rebuttal 2 was mitigated by a complete and effective closing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 1, which reframed the debate from "replacement" to "prioritization" and established the affirmative logic that "encounter is a precondition for education," thereby neutralizing Side A's depth argument by demonstrating that unseen documentaries have no democratic effect on youth who never open linear channels.</best_rebuttal>
